newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's red chip index soars on debut.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's red chip index soars on debut.

text.p: The Hang Seng red chip index soared on its debut on Monday, substantially outperforming the blue chip index, but many said this latest market barometer was not representative of the red chip, China-affiliated sector.
"The market was lifted by the launch of the red chip index," said Peter Lui in institutional sales at NAVA SC Securities, adding many of the constituents were very oversold last week.
The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index of 32 red chips opened at 2,732.85 on Monday morning, then roared ahead to close the morning session 6.2 percent higher at 2,836.38.
The index, which was backdated to January 4, 1993 with a base date of 1,000, added another 30 points in the afternoon to close 194.60 points, or 7.28 percent, higher at 2,867.32.
The blue chip Hang Seng Index closed 282.05 points or 2.00 percent higher at 14,394.60.

The index is weighted according to market capitalisation of each constituent stock. The five largest stocks in the index, China Resources Enterprise Ltd, Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd, China Overseas Land and Investment Ltd, Guangdong Investment Ltd and COSCO Pacific Ltd, all made good gains.
China Resources added HK$1.45 to HK$27.65 on heavy trade of HK$295.24 million and Shanghai Industrial put on HK$1.80 to HK$43.00.
China Overseas gained HK$0.35 to HK$5.20.
Guangdong Investment, the most actively traded issue in the market, advanced HK$0.80 to HK$10.25 on turnover of HK$693.95 million. COSCO Pacific gained HK$0.80 to HK$11.50.

"I agree with the way the index was done, with the criteria for stock selection, but at the moment I don't think it's really representative," said Lawrence Ang, head of China research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfel.
One of the criteria for selection was that a company was 35 percent held by a Chinese entity or a Hong Kong company that is controlled by a Chinese entity.
"CITIC Pacific should be included because it is the most typical red chip," said Ang.

In December 1996, members of CITIC Pacific's management acquired a 15.47 percent stake in the company from parent China International Trust and Investment Corp Hong Kong (Holdings) Ltd, thereby reducing the parent's stake to 26.45 percent from 41.92 percent.
"The two most exciting red chips Beijing Enterprises and China Everbright IHD are also not included," said Ang. "But I'm sure that one year later they will be in."
Beijing Enterprises, which was listed at the end of May, was the most heavily subscribed stock in the market's history, closed HK$3.00 higher at HK$48.40.
According to criteria drawn up by HSI Services which compiled the red chip index and the blue chip Hang Seng Index, a stock must have a trading record of at least 12 months.

China Everbright-IHD Pacific announced last week it had received the go-ahead from the Chinese government to acquire a 20 percent stake in Everbright Bank of China. The share closed at HK$12.60 before trading was suspended on Friday.
None of the stocks in this red chip index are constituents of the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index of 29 H shares.
H shares are issued with the full approval of the Chinese government by China-based subsidiaries of state owned enterprises.
The H share index closed 2.01 percent higher at 1,010.66.
